plot: On market day Hal sells his grandma's apples from his truck, but every car slows down, looks, says 'what a pity' and drives away; Grumpy dulls the 'too shiny' apples and Hal starts to think Wheelburg doesn't want him, while Pip (who came from the front) buys the first one; Bolt watches from across the street and sees every car is reading something at the back, so tall Bertha drives behind and reads the other side of Hal's two-sided board: 'SORRY! CLOSED TODAY! MOVING DAY!' (clue planted: Hal painted his apple sign on the back of his old moving sign); Grumpy flips it with his tow hook and every apple sells in an hour; lesson: before you feel sad, try to see it the way others see it; cliffhanger: the first snowflake lands on Bolt's hat.

script.title: Nobody Buys Hal's Apples!
script.description: Every car stops, looks... and drives away. Why? Inspector Bolt #26

set.place: Wheelburg Main Street on market day, Thursday afternoon until the market closes

beats.say: Fresh apples! Grandma's apples! Come and get them! Anybody?
A green car slowed down... looked... and drove away.
Two hours at market day. Not one apple sold!
It was Thursday afternoon. Market day on Main Street.
Hal had parked his big truck right in the middle.
Earlier that morning, he had hung up his brand new sign.
My new apple sign! Painted on the back of my old moving sign.
Two signs in one board. Very clever, Hal. Very clever.
I'll help you sell. I'm good with customers.
Really, Grumpy? You?
No. But I'm good at standing still. Same thing.
A blue car slowed down. It looked. Then it drove away too.
Bolt! Even you? Don't you like apples?
I love apples, Hal. I was only on my way to the bank.
But I'll come back. Hmm. Why didn't I stop just now?
Maybe my apples look bad. Grumpy, taste one.
Crunchy. Sweet. Too shiny. I don't like shiny.
Too shiny! That's it! Let's make them less shiny!
So Grumpy rubbed each apple with his dusty old cloth.
There. Dull and sad. Just like my weekends.
Thank you, Grumpy. Now they look a bit like potatoes.
Potatoes are honest food. Nobody says no to potatoes.
But the cars still slowed down, looked, and drove away.
Hi, Hal! Ooh, apples! Oh. Oh no. Sorry, Hal! Bye!
Turbo too? He said sorry! Sorry for what?
The market closes at five. I have only two hours left.
Maybe Wheelburg doesn't want a new stall. Or a new truck.
Wheelburg wants you. Wheelburg is just... slow.
Hal! Hal! I came to buy the shiniest apple!
Pip rolled right up to Hal's cab, from the front.
One apple, please! I'm your very first customer!
My first customer! Oh, Pip. Thank you.
But why is nobody else here? Your apples are yummy!
I don't know, Pip. Maybe they don't like big trucks.
I like big trucks! Big trucks carry the best things!
Bolt came back from the bank and parked across the street.
Let us watch for a minute. Quietly.
A red car slowed down. It looked. 'What a pity,' it said.
A small car slowed down. 'Oh, what a pity.' Off it went.
Every car slows down. Every car looks at the same spot.
And every car says, 'What a pity.' They are reading something!
Reading? But I didn't read anything. I came from the front.
Precisely, Pip. The cars come from the back.
Hurry, Bolt. Grandma's apples will go soft by tomorrow.
If I can't sell them today, I'll have to throw them away.
Hello, my darlings! What's all the fuss on Main Street?
Bertha! You're the tallest of us. Drive behind Hal's truck.
Tell us what the cars see. Every word.
Bertha rolled slowly behind the truck and looked at the open door.
Oh! Oh dear. Hal, sweetie... it says something very sad.
'SORRY! CLOSED TODAY! MOVING DAY!'
My old moving sign? But I see my apple sign!
You see the inside, Hal. The cars see the outside.
When you opened the door, your new sign turned to face you.
Two signs in one board! Very clever, Hal!
Ha! Not so clever after all.
So nobody was saying no to me. They thought I was closed!
And Turbo said sorry because he thought you were leaving again.
Let us flip it around. The right way. Ready?
Grumpy hooked the sign with his tow hook. And turned it. Clunk!
The very next car stopped. And the next. And the next!
Apples? Oh, how lovely! I thought you were closed, dear!
Hal! You're not moving away! Three apples, please! No, five!
In one hour, every single apple was sold.
Sold out! Grandma will be so proud!
They didn't dislike me. They just couldn't see what I meant.
Before you feel sad, try to see it the way others see it.
From the front AND from the back!
Same time next week, Hal? I'll bring my thirty kids!
I'll bring my cloth. For less shine.
As the market closed, something tiny and white floated down.
It landed right on Bolt's brown hat.
Cold. Soft. Is this... snow? In Wheelburg?
Snow? I've never driven on snow! Is it slippery?
What do you think Bolt will find next time? We'll find out in the next episode!
